title: Anxiety Disorders
subtitle: Case-based panic, generalized anxiety, phobias, course and treatment

cases.title: Case 1 — abrupt episodes at work
cases.scenario: 35-year-old woman had sudden breathlessness, dizziness, tachycardia, shaking and fear of a heart attack at her desk. Emergency ECG/blood work were unrevealing; two earlier episodes occurred in the prior month (pp.6–7).
questions: What diagnosis does the lecturer introduce after this case?
Which key post-attack course information is needed from the criteria slide?
answer: Persistent concern/worry or behavior change over at least a month, with recurrent unexpected attacks (p.12).
cases.memory: Original lecture case: PDF p.6 onward. Educational source case, not clinical advice.

cases.title: Case 2 — persistent worry
cases.scenario: 28-year-old married teacher worries about teaching performance and finances, with irritability, tension, restlessness and sleep difficulties (pp.13–14).
questions: Which lecture diagnosis follows this case?
Which duration and associated-symptom rules must be checked?
answer: At least six months of excessive worry and at least three of six associated symptoms (p.16).
cases.memory: Original lecture case: PDF p.13 onward. Educational source case, not clinical advice.

cases.title: Case 3 — avoidance after panic-like attacks
cases.scenario: 33-year-old woman has had attacks for eight years and avoids leaving home alone or busy places where escape might be difficult; needs accompaniment or her phone (pp.17–19).
questions: Which anxiety disorder does the lecture discuss next?
Name two relevant agoraphobic situation categories.
answer: Being outside home alone and standing in crowds/enclosed places (p.21).
cases.memory: Original lecture case: PDF p.17 onward. Educational source case, not clinical advice.

cases.title: Case 4 — fear of highway driving
cases.scenario: Lawyer experiences fear of fatal car accident when driving, especially highways, with racing heart, nausea and sweating, interfering with his commute.
cases.memory: Original lecture case: PDF p.22 onward. Educational source case, not clinical advice.

cases.title: Case 5 — public speaking and judgment
cases.scenario: 29-year-old computer programmer fears ridicule by colleagues and speaking in meetings, reporting palpitations, dry mouth, sweating and avoidance (pp.26–27).
questions: Which duration criterion is in the following slide?
answer: More than six months (p.29), which should be confirmed rather than inferred from the case text.
cases.memory: Original lecture case: PDF p.26 onward. Educational source case, not clinical advice.

coreShorts.q: Define fear and anxiety using the lecture.
coreShorts.a: Fear: appropriate response to known threat; anxiety: response to unknown/vague threat.

coreShorts.q: Name the four anxiety symptom domains in the diagram.
coreShorts.a: Emotional, cognitive, physiological, behavioral.

coreShorts.q: Name two physiologic anxiety symptoms in the diagram.
coreShorts.a: Increased heart rate and muscle tension.

coreShorts.q: Give four listed DSM-5 anxiety disorders.
coreShorts.a: Specific phobia, panic disorder, agoraphobia, generalized anxiety disorder (others also listed on p.5).

coreShorts.q: Summarize the sudden symptoms in Case 1.
coreShorts.a: Sudden dyspnea, dizziness, tachycardia, shaking and fear of death from a heart attack.

coreShorts.q: What was the reported frequency of Case 1's previous attacks?
coreShorts.a: Two additional episodes over the preceding month.

coreShorts.q: Name four physical panic symptoms from the slide.
coreShorts.a: For example breathlessness, palpitations, nausea and sweating.

coreShorts.q: Name two psychiatric panic symptoms.
coreShorts.a: Derealization/depersonalization and fear of losing control/dying.

coreShorts.q: Define anticipatory anxiety.
coreShorts.a: Persistent fear of further panic attacks.

coreShorts.q: What is the lecture's minimum panic-attack symptom threshold?
coreShorts.a: Four or more symptoms.

coreShorts.q: What concerns/changes after attacks contribute to Panic Disorder?
coreShorts.a: Persistent concern about more attacks, worry about implications, or significant behavior change for at least a month after an attack, in the setting of recurrent unexpected attacks.

coreShorts.q: Which worry domains occur in Case 2?
coreShorts.a: Professional teaching performance and financial security.

coreShorts.q: Name three accompanying GAD-case symptoms.
coreShorts.a: Tension, irritability, restlessness and/or sleep-onset difficulty.

coreShorts.q: State GAD duration and core worry pattern.
coreShorts.a: Excessive worry more days than not for at least six months across activities/events, difficult to control.

coreShorts.q: List six GAD associated symptoms.
coreShorts.a: Restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance.

coreShorts.q: How many associated GAD symptoms does the slide require?
coreShorts.a: Three or more of six.

coreShorts.q: What situations are avoided by Case 3?
coreShorts.a: Leaving home alone and crowded places such as malls, cinemas and banks where escape could be difficult.

coreShorts.q: Name the five agoraphobic situations.
coreShorts.a: Public transport, open spaces, enclosed places, lines/crowds, outside home alone.

coreShorts.q: How many situation categories and how long are in the agoraphobia criteria?
coreShorts.a: Two or more situations; typically six months or more.

coreShorts.q: What is the feared situation in Case 4?
coreShorts.a: Driving, particularly on highways.

coreShorts.q: Describe specific phobia criteria from p.24.
coreShorts.a: Marked immediate object/situation-specific fear, disproportionate, persistent ≥6 months with meaningful impairment/distress.

coreShorts.q: Name the specific-phobia subtypes.
coreShorts.a: Animal, natural environment, blood–injection–injury and situational.

coreShorts.q: What feared social situations trouble Case 5?
coreShorts.a: Meeting unfamiliar staff and public speaking, due to fear of ridicule.

coreShorts.q: List physical symptoms reported in Case 5.
coreShorts.a: Palpitations, dry mouth and sweating.

coreShorts.q: What is the Social Phobia duration rule in the lecture?
coreShorts.a: More than six months.

coreShorts.q: Which Social Anxiety specifier is listed?
coreShorts.a: Performance only.

coreShorts.q: Name three differential diagnoses for anxiety symptoms.
coreShorts.a: Substance/medication-induced anxiety, medical condition-induced anxiety and other anxiety disorders (examples).

coreShorts.q: Name two additional differential diagnoses from slide 32.
coreShorts.a: OCD and PTSD/acute stress disorder (also mood, delusional and adjustment disorders).

coreShorts.q: State the lecture's 12-month anxiety prevalence.
coreShorts.a: About 17%.

coreShorts.q: Give the lecture's prevalence figures for panic, phobia and GAD.
coreShorts.a: Panic 1.5–4%; phobia 10%; GAD 3–8%.

coreShorts.q: List four etiologic perspectives in the source diagram.
coreShorts.a: Biological, behavioral, cognitive, psychodynamic (also evolutionary and sociocultural).

coreShorts.q: List the three comorbidities highlighted.
coreShorts.a: Depression, alcohol/substance-use disorders and OCD.

coreShorts.q: Give the lecture's panic disorder long-term outcome proportions.
coreShorts.a: 30–40% symptom-free, ~50% mild symptoms, 10–20% significant symptoms.

coreShorts.q: What complicates anxiety disorder prognosis?
coreShorts.a: Comorbid alcohol or substance use and long-term relapsing course; monitor suicide risk.

coreShorts.q: Which medication categories are listed for GAD/PD/SAD?
coreShorts.a: Short-term benzodiazepines, SSRIs, SNRIs including venlafaxine and tricyclic antidepressants.

coreShorts.q: Which benzodiazepine side effects are noted?
coreShorts.a: Dependence and cognitive side effects.

coreShorts.q: Which conditions are buspirone and beta blockers assigned to?
coreShorts.a: Buspirone for GAD; beta blockers for social anxiety.

coreShorts.q: List the psychotherapy categories from p.40.
coreShorts.a: Cognitive, behavioral, and interpersonal psychotherapy.

coreShorts.q: Name three behavioral techniques from the source.
coreShorts.a: For example, systematic desensitization, graded exposure and relaxation.

coreShorts.q: What example illustrates virtual therapy?
coreShorts.a: Virtual crowded supermarket exposure for agoraphobia.

detailedShorts.q: Outline the panic-attack symptom clusters shown in the lecture.
detailedShorts.a: Cardiopulmonary: dyspnea/palpitations/chest discomfort. GI: nausea. Skin/systemic: sweating/chills/flushing. Neurologic: tremor/dizziness/paresthesia. Psychiatric: depersonalization/derealization and fear of dying/losing control; sudden onset.

detailedShorts.q: Describe the panic disorder criteria and exclusions as presented.
detailedShorts.a: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks; at least one followed for a month by persistent concern, worry about consequences or marked behavior change. A panic attack is described with ≥4 symptoms. Exclude effects of substances, medical conditions and a better explanatory psychiatric disorder.

detailedShorts.q: State GAD criteria listed in the original DSM-5 table.
detailedShorts.a: Excessive and difficult-to-control worry on more days than not for ≥6 months across areas; ≥3/6 symptoms (restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance); clinically significant impairment/distress; not due to substances/medical condition or another mental illness.

detailedShorts.q: Outline agoraphobia situations and persistence criteria.
detailedShorts.a: Marked fear of at least two of public transit, open spaces, enclosed spaces, queues/crowds, being outside alone; situations provoke fear and are avoided/endured with distress; disproportionate to actual danger; typically ≥6 months with impairment; exclude better explanations.

detailedShorts.q: Explain characteristic features and categories of specific phobia.
detailedShorts.a: Marked object- or situation-specific fear with almost immediate response, disproportionate to danger and sociocultural context, typically ≥6 months with impairment/distress; source specifiers: animals, natural environment, blood-injection-injury, situational (p.25).

detailedShorts.q: Describe the diagnostic features of social phobia and one specifier.
detailedShorts.a: Fear of social judgment or embarrassment, avoidance and fear out of proportion, >6 months with distress/impairment, exclusions; performance-only specifier mentioned on p.30.
Substance/medication or other medical causes; other anxiety disorders; somatic/illness anxiety; delusional, OCD, mood with anxious features, PTSD/acute stress, and adjustment anxiety.

detailedShorts.q: Outline the etiological categories diagrammed in the slide.
detailedShorts.a: Biological/genetic/autonomic/neurotransmitter and limbic factors; behavioral learning/conditioning; cognitive perceived control/interpretation; psychodynamic defense mechanisms; sociocultural pressures; evolutionary predisposition.

detailedShorts.q: What long-term outcomes and modifiers are described?
detailedShorts.a: Panic chronic with variable outcome (30–40% symptom-free, ~50% mild, 10–20% significant); agoraphobia may improve as panic improves, but can remain disabling without panic history; comorbidity worsens course and good premorbid function/brief duration favors prognosis.

detailedShorts.q: Summarize medications and psychotherapies in the source lecture.
detailedShorts.a: Outpatient usually; hospitalize selected severe risk/comorbidity. Medications include short-term benzodiazepines, SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs; buspirone for GAD, beta blockers for social anxiety, and resistant-case options. Psychotherapies include cognitive, behavioral, interpersonal, virtual, supportive and group approaches (pp.38–41).

rapid: Four or more during panic attack.
At least one month concern/worry/behavior change after an attack.
Fear almost always provoked by the specific object/situation.
Short-term/acute; dependence and cognitive side effects.
Social skills training for social anxiety.

explanation.heading: Fear versus anxiety
paragraphs: Fear في المحاضرة استجابة مناسبة لتهديد معروف (known threat)، بينما Anxiety استجابة لتهديد مبهم أو غير معروف (unknown/vague threat). العرض يميز كذلك normal وpathological anxiety دون معيار رقمي في شريحة التعريف.

explanation.heading: Symptom domains
paragraphs: في الرسم المرفق: Emotional = tension وapprehension؛ Cognitive = worry وأفكار عن عدم القدرة على المواجهة؛ Physiological = زيادة النبض وتوتر العضلات وautonomic arousal؛ Behavioral = avoidance وضعف إنجاز المهام وزيادة startle response.

explanation.heading: Anxiety disorders listed in the lecture
paragraphs: قائمة DSM-5 المصورة تتضمن specific phobia، panic disorder، agoraphobia، selective mutism، separation anxiety، GAD، unspecified/other specified anxiety، social anxiety، anxiety due to medical condition، وsubstance/medication-induced anxiety. هذه قائمة المحاضرة كما وردت في الشريحة.

explanation.heading: Case 1 — sudden attacks
paragraphs: سيدة عمرها 35 سنة ظهرت لها فجأة أثناء العمل صعوبة تنفّس ودوخة وتسرّع القلب ورعشة وخوف من موت بسبب أزمة قلبية. تقييم الطوارئ كان دون دليل مرض، وذكرت حدوث نوبتين أخريين خلال الشهر السابق (pp.6–7). يضع العرض الحالة تحت Panic Disorder؛ اكتمال جميع المعايير يعتمد على بقية المعطيات.

explanation.heading: Panic attack symptom groups
paragraphs: أعراض الـPanic في المحاضرة تشمل cardiopulmonary (dyspnea, palpitations, chest discomfort)، GI (nausea)، skin/systemic (sweating, chills/flushing)، neurologic (tremor, dizziness, tingling)، psychiatric (derealization/depersonalization, fear of death/loss of control). البداية abrupt وunpredictable.

explanation.heading: Panic disorder: concern and duration
paragraphs: بعد النوبات قد توجد Anticipatory Anxiety أي الخوف من تكرارها، وAvoidance Behaviors. تذكر المحاضرة شهرًا أو أكثر من القلق أو تغير السلوك بعد النوبة (pp.10–12)، مع تكرار النوبات غير المتوقعة حسب جدول DSM-5 المصور.

explanation.heading: Panic criteria and exclusions
paragraphs: تُسرد أربع أعراض على الأقل للـPanic Attack في شريحة المعايير، مع القلق/التجنّب واستمرار شهر أو أكثر للـPanic Disorder كما يوضّح الجدول المصور في p.12. يُستبعد أن تفسَّر الحالة بتعاطي/دواء أو مرض طبي أو اضطراب نفسي آخر.

explanation.heading: Case 2 — generalized worry
paragraphs: رجل 28 سنة، مدرس ومتزوج، يقلق باستمرار بشأن أدائه المهني والمال رغم استقراره، مع tension, irritability, restlessness وصعوبة النوم (pp.13–14). تضع المحاضرة الحالة تحت GAD؛ لم تذكر الحالة بذاتها مدة 6 أشهر، فلا يُفترض إثبات هذا الشرط من نص الحالة وحده.

explanation.heading: GAD DSM-5 criteria
paragraphs: جدول p.16: Excessive anxiety/worry في مجالات متعددة أكثر الأيام لمدة 6 أشهر على الأقل؛ صعوبة التحكم؛ ثلاثة أو أكثر من restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance؛ مع distress/impairment واستبعاد substance/medical condition أو اضطراب نفسي آخر.

explanation.heading: Case 3 — fear of being away from home
paragraphs: سيدة 33 سنة بدأت لديها نوبات تشبه الـPanic قبل 8 سنوات؛ لاحقًا تخاف من وجود النوبة خارج المنزل، وتحتاج هاتفًا أو مرافقًا، وتتجنب المولات والسينما والبنوك والأماكن التي يصعب الخروج منها (pp.17–19). يضع العرض الحالة تحت Agoraphobia.

explanation.heading: Agoraphobia DSM-5 criteria
paragraphs: الرسم p.21 يطلب خوفًا/قلقًا واضحًا من موقفين أو أكثر من: public transport، open spaces، enclosed places، standing in line/crowd، outside home alone. المواقف تُتجنَّب أو تُحتمل بقلق، والخوف disproportionate ويستمر عادة ≥6 أشهر مع impairment، واستبعاد التفسير الأفضل باضطراب آخر.

explanation.heading: Case 4 — situational phobia
paragraphs: محام يخاف بشدة من القيادة على الطرق السريعة ويخشى موتًا في حادث، مع racing heart وغثيان وتعرق؛ يؤثر ذلك على الوصول للعمل بعد انتقال المكتب (p.22). يقدم العرض الحالة كـSpecific Phobia (situational).

explanation.heading: Specific phobia diagnostic features
paragraphs: الصورة p.24 تذكر fear/anxiety من object/situation محدد، استجابة قلق فورية عادة، خوف غير متناسب مع الخطر/السياق، استمرارية 6 أشهر أو أكثر، وdistress أو impairment مهم. الشريحة التالية تذكر استبعاد اضطراب نفسي آخر.

explanation.heading: Specific phobia specifiers
paragraphs: تسرد المحاضرة أنواعًا: animals، natural environment، blood–injection–injury، situational. مثال قيادة السيارة في الحالة الرابعة situational.

explanation.heading: Case 5 — fear of scrutiny
paragraphs: موظفة كمبيوتر 29 سنة تخشى التفاعل مع أناس جدد والتحدث أمام مجموعة بسبب احتمال السخرية أو الإحراج، وتظهر palpitations, dry mouth, sweating، وبدأت تتجنب الاجتماعات (pp.26–27). يسمي العرض الحالة Social Anxiety Disorder؛ مدة 6 أشهر مطلوبة بحسب معايير p.29، ولا ترد مدة محددة في الحالة.

explanation.heading: Social anxiety criteria
paragraphs: تتضمن معايير Social Phobia قلقًا من judgment/scrutiny في المواقف الاجتماعية، وخوفًا من ظهور القلق بما يسبب الحرج، وتجنّبًا وسلوكًا غير متناسب مع الخطر، واستمرارًا لأكثر من 6 أشهر، وdistress/impairment. يذكر العرض performance-only specifier في p.30.

explanation.heading: Differential diagnosis
paragraphs: قائمة Differential Diagnosis في pp.31–32: substance/medication-induced anxiety، medical conditions، other anxiety disorders، somatic symptom، illness anxiety، delusional disorder، OCD، mood disorders with anxious features، PTSD/acute stress، adjustment disorder with anxious features.

explanation.heading: Epidemiology: lecture figures
paragraphs: بحسب شريحة المحاضرة: anxiety disorders أكثر مجموعات الاضطرابات النفسية شيوعًا؛ one in four ever meets criteria، نحو 17% 12-month prevalence. الأرقام المعروضة: panic disorder 1.5–4%، phobia 10%، GAD 3–8%. النساء أكثر تأثرًا حسب المحاضرة. هذه الأرقام تعليمية من المصدر دون تحديث خارجي.

explanation.heading: Etiology diagram
paragraphs: الرسم p.34 يقسّم etiologies إلى Biological (genetics, autonomic and neurotransmitter factors, amygdala/prefrontal)، Behavioral (observational and conditioning learning)، Cognitive (perceived control and interpretations)، Psychodynamic وSociocultural perspectives. يُراجع الرسم الأصلي عند الدراسة ولا يُنشر هنا.

explanation.heading: Comorbid conditions
paragraphs: المحاضرة تسرد Depression 40–80%، Alcohol/substance use disorders 20–40%، وOCD كـComorbidity. استخدم النسب كما في الشريحة ولا تُعدَّل بمراجع حديثة أثناء المذاكرة.

explanation.heading: Course and prognosis: panic and agoraphobia
paragraphs: المحاضرة تصف Panic Disorder بأنه chronic مع course متغير؛ أرقام المتابعة: 30–40% بلا أعراض، نحو 50% أعراض خفيفة، 10–20% أعراض مهمة. تحسّن panic قد يحسّن agoraphobia المصاحب؛ agoraphobia دون panic قد يكون مزمنًا ومعيقًا.

explanation.heading: General prognosis and risk
paragraphs: غالبية اضطرابات القلق لها مسارات طويلة مع انتكاسات، وتؤكد المحاضرة الانتباه لخطر الانتحار. Comorbid alcohol/substance disorders تُعقّد المسار؛ good premorbid functioning وقِصر المدة يرتبطان بتكهن أفضل.

explanation.heading: Treatment setting and medications
paragraphs: تذكر المحاضرة غالبًا outpatient مع استثناءات تحتاج hospitalization بسبب الانتحار أو الأمراض المصاحبة؛ ومن الأدوية لـGAD/PD/SAD: Benzodiazepines للحالات الحادة والاستخدام القصير (dependence وcognitive adverse effects)، SSRIs، SNRIs مثل venlafaxine، وTCAs.

explanation.heading: Other pharmacologic options
paragraphs: تسرد شريحة المحاضرة Buspirone لـGAD، Beta blockers للـSocial Anxiety، وAntipsychotics/Anticonvulsants للحالات المقاومة؛ هذه مراجعة لما في السلايد وليست توصية علاجية مستقلة.

explanation.heading: Psychotherapy
paragraphs: الـPsychotherapy المذكور يشمل Cognitive therapy لتحدي maladaptive thoughts، وBehavioral therapy (reinforcement, systematic desensitization, flooding, implosion, graded exposure, response prevention, thought stopping, relaxation) وInterpersonal psychotherapy مع مهارات العلاقات.

explanation.heading: Virtual and supportive approaches
paragraphs: Virtual therapy قد تحاكي المواقف مثل crowded supermarket لدى مريض agoraphobia، وتكون مفيدة عندما يصعب تمثيل الموقف في العيادة. تذكر المحاضرة أيضًا supportive therapy وgroup therapy.

explanation.heading: Panic attack versus Panic Disorder on the source DSM-5 slide
paragraphs: تفرّق الصورة بين Panic Attack كحدث، وPanic Disorder الذي يتطلب recurrent unexpected attacks ثم استمرار القلق بشأن نوبات أخرى أو النتائج أو تغير السلوك شهرًا على الأقل بعد واحدة منها. وتذكر الصورة أن PD وAgoraphobia أصبحا تشخيصين منفصلين في DSM-5. لا يكفي حدوث الأعراض الجسمية وحدها لإثبات جميع شروط الاضطراب.

explanation.heading: GAD: distinguish lecture case from formal diagnosis
paragraphs: الحالة الثانية في الصفحات 13–14 تُستخدم تمثيلًا لـGAD لكنها لا تذكر مدة مستقلة قدرها ستة أشهر. لذلك لا تستنتج مدة 6 أشهر من الحالة؛ راجع قاعدة مدة القلق (على مدار 6 أشهر وأكثر الأيام) والـ3/6 أعراض في جدول DSM-5 المصور في هذه الصفحة.

explanation.heading: Specific-phobia figure and case interpretation
paragraphs: تشرح الصورة خمس صفات أساسية للخوف المحدد: object/situation واضح، قلق فوري غالبًا عند التعرض، خوف غير متناسب مع الخطر أو السياق، استمرار عادة 6 أشهر أو أكثر، وتأثير وظيفي/معاناة معتبرة. حالة القيادة في الصفحة 22 مثال تعليمي للنوع Situational المذكور في الصفحة 25.

explanation.heading: Etiology figure: learning, cognition and neurobiology
paragraphs: يذكر الرسم عوامل Biological مثل الوراثة والجهاز العصبي الذاتي والتغيرات في norepinephrine/serotonin/GABA/glutamate والأميغدالا وقشرة الفص الجبهي. Behavioral theory تتضمن observational learning وclassical/operant conditioning. Cognitive approach يركز على ضعف perceived control والتفسيرات غير الدقيقة. كما يسرد psychodynamic وevolutionary وsociocultural perspectives؛ هذه نظريات واردة في المصدر وليست استنتاجًا مستقلًا.

explanation.heading: Psychotherapy table: source technique comparisons
paragraphs: Cognitive therapy تستهدف maladaptive thoughts، بينما Behavioral therapy تذكر graded exposure وsystematic desensitization وrelaxation وغيرها. Interpersonal psychotherapy في المحاضرة تركز على تدريب المهارات الاجتماعية لـSocial Anxiety Disorder. الصفحة التالية تضيف virtual, supportive وgroup therapy.

explanation.heading: Case 5 and duration evidence
paragraphs: الـCase 5 في الصفحتين 26–27 يوضح Social Anxiety لكنه لا يذكر مدة محددة للخوف؛ أمّا معيار المحاضرة فهو أكثر من 6 أشهر. لا تُضف المدة إلى بيانات الحالة من عندك، وافصل بين تسمية الحالة التعليمية والتحقق من كل criterion.

mcqs.question: How does the lecture distinguish fear from anxiety?
options: Fear concerns an unknown threat; anxiety a known threat
Fear is an appropriate response to a known threat; anxiety to a vague/unknown threat
mcqs.rationale: Fear is linked to known threat and anxiety to unknown/vague threat.

mcqs.question: Which is classified as a cognitive symptom of anxiety in the diagram?
mcqs.rationale: The diagram places worry under cognitive symptoms.

mcqs.question: Which is a behavioral symptom shown in the anxiety diagram?
mcqs.rationale: Avoidance is in the behavioral box.

mcqs.question: Which disorder appears in the slide's DSM-5 anxiety list?
mcqs.rationale: Social Anxiety Disorder appears in the list.

mcqs.question: Which symptom in Case 1 started suddenly at work?
mcqs.rationale: The case describes sudden dyspnea and tachycardia.

mcqs.question: What did the emergency evaluation reveal in Case 1?
options: No sign of illness on ECG and routine tests
mcqs.rationale: The slide reports unremarkable ECG and routine blood work.

mcqs.question: Which is a psychiatric symptom among the listed panic symptoms?
mcqs.rationale: Derealization/depersonalization appear in the psychiatric symptom group.

mcqs.question: Panic symptoms in the lecture are described as:
options: Always triggered by a single object
mcqs.rationale: Abrupt/unpredictable is explicitly stated.

mcqs.question: How many panic-attack symptoms are specified on the slide?
mcqs.rationale: The panic-attack threshold on the slide is four or more symptoms.

mcqs.question: What post-attack duration is shown in the panic disorder DSM-5 table?
mcqs.rationale: The image says at least one attack followed by at least one month of concern, worry, or behavior change.

mcqs.question: Which phrase best describes anticipatory anxiety?
mcqs.rationale: Anticipatory anxiety is fear of subsequent attacks.

mcqs.question: What kinds of worry are emphasized in Case 2?
mcqs.rationale: The teacher worries about teaching performance and loss of money.

mcqs.question: The minimum duration specified for GAD worry in the DSM-5 table is:
mcqs.rationale: The source table specifies at least 6 months on more days than not.

mcqs.question: How many of the six listed associated GAD symptoms are required in the table?
mcqs.rationale: The source table specifies three or more of six.

mcqs.question: Which is included among GAD associated symptoms?
mcqs.rationale: Muscle tension is one of six associated symptoms.

mcqs.question: Why does the woman in Case 3 avoid crowded places?
options: Fear of an attack where escape may be difficult
mcqs.rationale: Case 3 links avoidance to fear of attacks outside home/difficulty escaping.

mcqs.question: Agoraphobia criteria in the lecture require fear about how many listed situation categories?
mcqs.rationale: The p.21 table specifies two or more of five situations.

mcqs.question: Which is one of the five listed agoraphobic situations?
options: Standing in line or being in a crowd
mcqs.rationale: Standing in line/being in a crowd is listed.

mcqs.question: The usual persistence threshold on the agoraphobia slide is:
mcqs.rationale: The slide specifies typically 6 months or more.

mcqs.question: Case 4 is centered on fear of:
mcqs.rationale: The lawyer fears driving, particularly highways.

mcqs.question: Specific phobia commonly produces:
options: Immediate fear when exposed to the object or situation
mcqs.rationale: The photographed criteria note nearly always immediate fear/anxiety.

mcqs.question: Which is listed as a specific-phobia subtype?
mcqs.rationale: Blood–injection–injury is one of the listed specifiers.

mcqs.question: Case 5 is most concerned about:
mcqs.rationale: Fear of ridicule/embarrassment is the core of the source case.

mcqs.question: The duration criterion on the Social Phobia slide is:
mcqs.rationale: The lecture slide states duration more than 6 months.

mcqs.question: Which specifier is explicitly mentioned for Social Anxiety?
mcqs.rationale: Performance-only (performance anxiety) is listed.

mcqs.question: Which belongs to the differential diagnosis list?
mcqs.rationale: Substance/medication-induced anxiety is listed in the differential.

mcqs.question: According to the lecture, the approximate 12-month prevalence of anxiety disorders is:
mcqs.rationale: The epidemiology slide says about 17%.

mcqs.question: Which comorbid condition is explicitly listed?
mcqs.rationale: Depression is listed with 40–80% in the lecture.

mcqs.question: According to the lecture's long-term panic disorder estimates, what proportion are symptom-free?
mcqs.rationale: The source slide gives approximately 30–40% symptom-free.

mcqs.question: Which factor in the lecture is associated with more favorable prognosis?
mcqs.rationale: Good premorbid functioning and brief duration tend toward a favorable course.

mcqs.question: Which medication class is described for acute/short-term anxiety in the lecture?
mcqs.rationale: The slide mentions benzodiazepines for acute cases/short term, with dependence and cognitive side effects.

mcqs.question: Which SNRI is named in the treatment slide?
mcqs.rationale: Venlafaxine is explicitly named as an SNRI.

mcqs.question: Which drug is assigned to GAD in the lecture?
mcqs.rationale: The treatment slide lists buspirone for GAD.

mcqs.question: Which is included among the behavioral techniques in the lecture?
mcqs.rationale: Graded exposure appears in the behavioral therapy list.

mcqs.question: The virtual-therapy example in the lecture depicts:
options: A surgical theatre for pain control
A crowded supermarket scenario for agoraphobia
mcqs.rationale: The slide explicitly gives a supermarket crowded-space scenario.

mcqs.question: According to the image-only DSM-5 table, Panic Disorder and agoraphobia are:
mcqs.rationale: The p.12 table states that PD and agoraphobia are unlinked in DSM-5.

mcqs.question: In the GAD criteria table, the anxiety and worry must be:
mcqs.rationale: The second criterion in the source table is difficulty controlling worry.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a formal exclusion in the GAD source table?
options: Occurrence in more than one life area
A different medical condition or substance effect
mcqs.rationale: The p.16 image specifies substance or medical causes and other mental disorders as exclusions.

mcqs.question: Agoraphobic situations, according to the source image, generally:
options: Almost always provoke fear or anxiety
Must always involve a specific animal
mcqs.rationale: The image says agoraphobic situations almost always provoke fear or anxiety.

mcqs.question: Which criterion from the specific-phobia slide addresses actual danger?
options: Fear is proportionate to actual danger
Fear is out of proportion to the actual danger or sociocultural context
mcqs.rationale: The p.24 criteria directly require fear to be disproportionate.

mcqs.question: According to the etiology image, what is a cognitive contribution to anxiety?
mcqs.rationale: The source diagram lists lack of perceived control and irrational interpretation in its cognitive column.

mcqs.question: Observing anxious behaviours in parents is placed under which etiologic explanation?
mcqs.rationale: The behavioral column gives observational learning from parents.

mcqs.question: Overactivity of which neurotransmitter is connected to onset of panic attacks in the lecture figure?
mcqs.rationale: The biological column connects norepinephrine overactivity to panic attacks.

mcqs.question: Which comorbidity range is specifically given for alcohol and substance use disorders?
mcqs.rationale: The source comorbidity slide lists alcohol/substance use disorders at 20–40%.

mcqs.question: Which risk is linked to benzodiazepines on the slide?
mcqs.rationale: The p.38 treatment slide names dependence and cognitive side effects.

mcqs.question: In the lecture, interpersonal psychotherapy for social anxiety focuses on:
mcqs.rationale: The psychotherapy slide specifically highlights interpersonal skills training.

mcqs.question: Why is virtual therapy described as useful in the source?
options: It is solely for memory testing
It recreates situations difficult to reproduce near the clinic
mcqs.rationale: The source says virtual exposure can simulate situations hard to reproduce inside or near an office.
